data.one_liner: Extends Riverpod ref types with helpers like caching, debouncing, and auto-refreshing.
data.what_it_does: Provides useful extension methods on Riverpod ref types to easily add common functionalities to providers. Features include caching data durations, debouncing computations, auto-refreshing intervals, and refreshing when returning to the foreground or when the network becomes available.
use_when: You want to prevent a provider from being disposed immediately using cacheFor or cacheDataFor.
You need automatic periodic refreshing or network-aware refreshing for your providers.
You want to debounce provider computations or refresh AsyncNotifiers when the app returns to the foreground.
avoid_when: You are using Riverpod version 2 (version 3.0.0 requires Riverpod 3).
You do not use Riverpod in your application.
strengths: Simplifies common provider lifecycle and caching patterns in Riverpod.
Includes helpful connectivity and lifecycle-aware refresh triggers.
Compatible with both traditional providers and code generation.
weaknesses: Strictly tied to Riverpod 3 in version 3.0.0.
Some methods are limited to specific ref types like AsyncNotifier.
data.setup_notes: Simply add the package dependency and import it in your Dart files where Riverpod ref is used.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: Riverpod core features can sometimes handle provider behaviors natively without community extension wrappers.
